units.text: The 2012 Statistical Abstract's Table 366 lists state high point elevations but does not provide a count or proportion of states exceeding 1,000 ft.

citations.title: Table 366. Extreme and Mean Elevations by State and Other Areas

judgement.reason: The passages show Table 366 contains state highest point names and elevations (e.g., McKinley 20,320 ft), and its listed columns are only elevation data, with no count or proportion of states exceeding 1,000 ft.

units.text: Visual Capitalist's table, citing USGS/Census data, reports a median state high point of 4,588.5 ft, with 37 states above 2,000 ft and 22 above 5,000 ft, indicating most states exceed 1,000 ft, but the source does not explicitly state this proportion.

citations.title: Mapped: The Highest Point in Every U.S. State

judgement.reason: The median of 4,588.5 ft and counts of 37 states above 2,000 ft and 22 above 5,000 ft are supported; however, the passages do not show any citation to USGS/Census data.
